title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, function/tool calling, roles/stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Close remaining behavior gaps between Redwood's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions layer and upstream OpenAI semantics for: 1) streaming stability under bursty concurrent streams, 2) deterministic handling of roles and stop sequences, 3) correct emittance of logprobs and token-level metadata in both streaming and non-streaming flows, and 4) structured/JSON response formatting and tool/function calling glue. This PR consolidates previous parity iterations and addresses several user-reported regressions (see linked Linear tasks). Summary of changes: - Streaming: introduce backpressure-aware stream multiplexer with prioritized flush for function/tool call payloads; fix race where final chunk was dropped under high-concurrency; add jittered retry for transient client disconnects. - Roles/stop handling: canonicalize role normalization (user/system/assistant) at the API boundary and enforce stop-token matching semantics identical to OpenAI (support multi-sequence stop arrays, prefix vs token matching behavior). - Logprobs: ensure logprobs are computed and emitted for both streaming partial tokens and final response; annotate token positions consistently and include `top_logprobs` key when requested. - Structured output: enforce content-type and JSON-safe framing in streaming SSE chunks; add deterministic content-disposition for tool/function calls and structured output fields (name, arguments, metadata). - Compatibility layer: expand OpenAI-compat adapter to accept `messages` with `role` aliases, forward `function_call` hints to runtime, and map Redwood internal model variants to OpenAI model names with explicit fallbacks. - Tests & docs: comprehensive unit/integration tests added; updated API docs and examples for function calling and structured outputs. Backwards compatibility & rollout: default behavior is unchanged for existing clients; new strict stop and role semantics are gated behind a compat flag `openai_parity: true` for rollout. We will flip the flag for beta customers and monitor for regressions before global rollout. Related Linear tasks: ENG-1221 (streaming stability), ENG-1337 (openai parity: stop/logprobs), ENG-1405 (structured output docs).
